Answer: C
Reason: The frontal chest X-ray (Figure 1a) shows a large opacity in the right hemithorax that obscures the right heart border and diaphragm, consistent with a posterior mediastinal mass compressing the right lung. The lateral view (Figure 1b) confirms the posterior location of the mass. There is no significant deviation of the trachea or displacement of the cardiac silhouette to the left, which helps distinguish this from anterior mediastinal masses or those causing massive shift.
